Activités visant à prouver la validité ou la faisabilité technique d'un concept par l'application de méthodologies scientifiques et d'ingénierie. Le travail dans cette famille de métiers a généralement pour objectif de démontrer, par des tests ou des analyses, la performance et le potentiel de mise en œuvre d'un concept.

 Job Description 
 Main Responsibilities 
 Conceptual or theoretical activities that deals with the study/research and application of electricity, electronics, and electromagnetism.
 Developing in-depth knowledge of a technical discipline. Uses prior experience and acquired technical expertise to execute policy/strategy.
 In-depth understanding of key business drivers; uses this understanding to accomplish own work. In-depth understanding of how work of own team integrates with other teams and contributes to the area.
 Uses some level of judgment and has ability to propose different solutions outside of set parameters but with guidance. Uses prior experience and on-the-job training to solve straightforward tasks. Has access to technical skills and analytic thinking required to solve problems. May use multiple internal sources outside of own team to arrive at decisions.
 A job at this level is likely to be an individual contributor with proven interpersonal skills or an early people leader who can hire and develop talent. Provides informal guidance to new team members
 Firmware Development: Design, develop, and maintain robust, real-time embedded software for microprocessor-based protection relays using C/C++.
 Multidisciplinary Collaboration: Work closely with Protection Engineers to implement complex mathematical algorithms into efficient, embedded-ready code.
 Performance Optimization: Optimize firmware performance for real-time execution, focusing on low-latency data processing required for protection functions and IEC 61850 communication stacks.
 Validation & Debugging:  Testing and profiling to ensure stability under extreme grid conditions.
 Cybersecurity Integration: Implement secure coding practices and security features within the firmware architecture in compliance with IEC 62443.
 Use AI coding assistants for embedded C/C++ generation, refactoring, and unit test scaffolding
 Write precise specs/prompts so agentic AI produces bounded, verifiable code changes
 Validate AI-generated code against real-time timing and memory constraints
 Apply AI-assisted static analysis for safety-critical code review
Required Qualifications 
 Education: Master’s degree in Embedded Systems, Computer Science, or Electrical Engineering.
 Expert-level proficiency in C and C++ for embedded environments.
 Knowledge of power system protection principles or digital signal processing (DSP).
 Proficiency in Python for Test automation
 Knowledge on GitHub
 Experience with Real-Time Operating Systems (VxWorks., FreeRTOS, QNX, or Embedded Linux).
 Language: Proficiency in English; French is mandatory for local collaboration.
 Desired Characteristics 
 Experience with Model-Based Design (e.g., MATLAB/Simulink coder).
 Familiarity with Agile/Scrum development methodologies and CI/CD pipelines for firmware.
 Prior experience in the Energy, Industrial, or Aerospace sectors.
 Strong oral and written communication skills. Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems. Ability to document, plan, market, and execute programs. Established project management skills.
 For candidates applying to a Canadian-based position, the pay range for this position is between $92,300 and $142,000 CAD. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set.
  Bonus eligibility: Discretionary Annual Bonus
  This posting is for an existing vacancy.
 -----
 Responsabilités Essentielles
 Activités conceptuelles ou théoriques liées à l'étude/recherche et à l'application de l'électricité, de l'électronique et de l'électromagnétisme.
 Développement d'une connaissance approfondie d'une discipline technique. Utilisation de l'expérience antérieure et de l'expertise technique acquise pour exécuter les politiques/stratégies.
 Compréhension approfondie des principaux facteurs de réussite de l'entreprise ; utilisation de cette compréhension pour accomplir son travail. Compréhension approfondie de la manière dont le travail de sa propre équipe s'intègre avec d'autres équipes et contribue au domaine.
 Utilisation d'un certain niveau de jugement et capacité à proposer différentes solutions en dehors des paramètres établis, mais avec supervision. Utilisation de l'expérience antérieure et de la formation sur le tas pour résoudre des tâches simples. Accès aux compétences techniques et à la pensée analytique nécessaires pour résoudre les problèmes. Peut utiliser plusieurs sources internes en dehors de sa propre équipe pour prendre des décisions.
 À ce niveau, le poste est probablement celui d'un contributeur individuel doté de compétences interpersonnelles avérées ou d'un leader débutant capable de recruter et de développer des talents. Fournit des conseils informels aux nouveaux membres de l'équipe.
 Développement de firmware : Concevoir, développer et maintenir des logiciels embarqués temps réel robustes pour des relais de protection à base de microprocesseurs en utilisant C/C++.
 Collaboration multidisciplinaire : Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les ingénieurs protection pour implémenter des algorithmes mathématiques complexes dans un code efficace et prêt pour l'embarqué.
 Optimisation des performances : Optimiser les performances du firmware pour une exécution en temps réel, en se concentrant sur le traitement de données à faible latence requis pour les fonctions de protection et les piles de communication IEC 61850.
 Validation et débogage : Tests et profilage pour garantir la stabilité dans des conditions de réseau extrêmes.
 Intégration de la cybersécurité : Implémenter des pratiques de codage sécurisé et des fonctionnalités de sécurité au sein de l'architecture du firmware, conformément à la norme IEC 62443.
 Utiliser des assistants de codage IA pour la génération de code C/C++ embarqué, le refactoring et l'échafaudage de tests unitaires.
 Rédiger des spécifications/prompts précis afin que l'IA agentique produise des changements de code délimités et vérifiables.
 Valider le code généré par l'IA par rapport aux contraintes de temps réel et de mémoire.
 Appliquer l'analyse statique assistée par l'IA pour la révision de code critique pour la sécurité.
 Qualifications requises
 Formation : Master en Systèmes Embarqués, Informatique ou Génie Électrique
 Niveau Expert en  C et du C++ pour les environnements embarqués.
 Connaissance des principes de protection des systèmes électriques ou du traitement numérique du signal (DSP).
 Maîtrise de Python pour l'automatisation des tests.
 Connaissance de GitHub.
 Expérience avec les systèmes d'exploitation temps réel (VxWorks, FreeRTOS, QNX ou Linux embarqué).
 Langue : Maîtrise de l'anglais ; le français est obligatoire pour la collaboration locale.
 Caractéristiques souhaitées
 Expérience en conception basée sur les modèles (par exemple, MATLAB/Simulink Coder).
 Familiarité avec les méthodologies de développement Agile/Scrum et les pipelines CI/CD pour le firmware.
 Expérience préalable dans les secteurs de l'énergie, de l'industrie ou de l'aérospatiale.
 Solides compétences en communication orale et écrite. Capacité démontrée à analyser et à résoudre des problèmes. Capacité à documenter, planifier, commercialiser et exécuter des programmes. Compétences établies en gestion de projet.
  Poste ouvert aux personnes en situation de handicap. Un référent handicap est présent sur chaque site en France.

 Nous fabriquons et fournissons des médicaments et des vaccins fiables et de haute qualité afin de répondre aux besoins des patients et de soutenir notre performance.
 Notre réseau de 37 sites de production de médicaments et de vaccins a livré 1,7 milliard d’unités de médicaments et 409 millions de doses de vaccins en 2024, contribuant ainsi à améliorer la santé de millions de personnes. Notre chaîne d’approvisionnement n’est pas seulement au cœur de nos activités ; elle est essentielle pour mettre nos innovations à la disposition des patients aussi rapidement et efficacement que possible. Les technologies de pointe transforment la façon dont nous fabriquons les médicaments et les vaccins, nous permettant d’accroître la rapidité, la qualité et l’ampleur de l’approvisionnement en produits.
 Nous recherchons les meilleurs talents et les plus grandes expertises pour nous accompagner dans notre parcours vers la fabrication de produits de plus en plus complexes. Nous tirons parti des technologies de fabrication intelligente, notamment la robotique, les solutions numériques et l’intelligence artificielle, afin de mieux servir les patients.

 Pourquoi GSK? 
 Chez GSK, nous valorisons l’inclusion ainsi que la diversité des perspectives, des idées et des expériences. Nous souhaitons créer un environnement où chacun peut se sentir accueilli, valorisé et en mesure de donner le meilleur de lui-même.

Allier science, technologie et talent pour vaincre ensemble la maladie.

About Moment Energy 
 Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it. 
 Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone. 
 The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy. 
 Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact. 
 We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale. 
 Now is the moment. Join us. 
 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a Software Engineering Co-op to join our Engineering team starting in January 2027. In this role, you will support the development of the cloud platform that powers our battery management systems and energy storage products. 
 You will work on both front-end and back-end development while collaborating with engineers across hardware and software teams. This is a great opportunity for a student who wants to gain hands-on experience building scalable software systems for real-world energy infrastructure.

 Develop front-end web interfaces for the battery management system (BMS) cloud portal

 Design and implement database schemas to support platform functionality

 Develop unit tests and integration tests to ensure system reliability and stability

 Basic understanding of databases and data modeling 
 Interest in cloud platforms, IoT systems, and connected hardware 
 Experience with version control systems such as Git 
 Strong problem-solving and analytical skills 
 Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced engineering environment 
 The Experience You’ll Gain: 
 Hands-on experience developing software for real-world energy infrastructure 
 Exposure to cloud platforms, IoT systems, and hardware-software integration 
 Mentorship from experienced software and systems engineers 
 The opportunity to contribute to technology supporting the clean energy transition

 Paid Time Off: Co-op’s receive three paid days off per term

 Today, we’re delivering 5x the energy density and have all the certifications needed to ship energy independence to the world. 
 Be part of a mission-driven company focused on creating sustainable energy solutions and making a positive impact on the world. 
 Collaborate closely with passionate co-founders and a team committed to innovation and excellence.

We especially welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, members of racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+. 
 —--- 
 Our Values 
 Our values are key to how we show up every day at Moment Energy! We keep them in the forefront of what we do, and they’re used everywhere. We refer to them when we have tough decisions to make, we give shoutouts based on living out these values, and we include them as part of our performance reviews.

 Safety is our Foundation 
 We prioritize the safety of our products, customers, employees, and the general public above all else. From the workshop to the field, we maintain the highest standards for our batteries in testing manufacturing and deployment, and daily operations. Safety is not only about procedures—it is about vigilance, responsibility, and speaking up when something does not feel right.

 We’re self-starters that proactively embrace new challenges along with personal and collective ownership of responsibilities in the organization. We focus on growth, not titles, and we do what needs to be done.

Job Description Summary 
We are looking for a senior OT cybersecurity engineer to join the Grid Automation Cybersecurity Center of Excellence (COE). The COE is a new central team within the Grid Automation OT Cybersecurity Product Line, and it owns how cybersecurity is delivered on Grid Automation projects worldwide.
This is a hands-on role. You will design, build, configure, test and, where needed, commission security solutions on complex utility and industrial projects. You will then turn that work into the standards, templates, scripts and training that regional teams use on every project that follows.
You will be the recognized technical owner for a set of solutions in the GA cybersecurity portfolio. Regional teams will come to you when a project goes beyond their experience.
Projects are grouped into three tiers, and the region manages the customer relationship on all of them. On complex (Tier 1) projects, the COE leads cybersecurity execution. On standard (Tier 2) projects, the region delivers using the COE toolkit, with COE support and training. On routine (Tier 3) projects, the region works independently and the COE reviews key milestones. 
You will also make delivery faster and more consistent by automating repeatable work in PowerShell and using frontier AI models to speed up documentation, requirements mapping and configuration reviews. 
 Job Description 
 Roles and Responsibilities
  Project Execution 
 Lead the cybersecurity workstream on Tier 1 projects end to end: requirements review, security architecture, detailed design, build, configuration, FAT, SAT, commissioning and handover.
 Produce the project security deliverables: security plan, zone and conduit model, risk assessment, hardening records, test procedures and reports, and the security handover package.
 Map customer requirements to contract scope early, flag deviations as they arise, and give project managers the technical basis for change orders.
  Execution Standards & Toolkit 
 Act as the technical owner (Expert) for an assigned set of COE competencies. Set the reference configuration for each and keep it current with product and partner releases.
 Build the GA execution toolkit as a by-product of delivery: reference architectures, configuration baselines, build checklists, PowerShell scripts, how-to guides, test procedures and templates.
 Automation 
 Write and maintain PowerShell scripts and modules that automate repeatable execution tasks.
 Build automated checks that compare as-built systems against the COE reference baselines and produce the evidence for milestone reviews, FAT and SAT.
 Use frontier AI models to speed up execution work.
 Competency building & Specialist Support 
 Design and deliver structured technical training for regional engineers, from foundation to advanced level, on the solutions you own.
 Track IEC 62443, NERC CIP, NIS2, CRA, IEC 62351 and regional mandates, and translate new requirements into execution checklists and deliverables.
 Required Qualifications
 Bachelor's or master's degree in Electrical, Electronics or Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent experience, with minumum 8 years in industrial automation or the energy sector, including at least 5 years of hands-on OT cybersecurity delivery on customer projects.
 Applied knowledge of IEC 62443 on real projects (especially parts 3-2, 3-3 and 2-4), working knowledge of NERC CIP, NIS2, CRA, IEC 62351 and NIST, and a sound understanding of substation and grid automation systems and protocols such as IEC 61850, DNP3, IEC 60870-5-104 and Modbus.
 Expert, hands-on skills in at least three of these areas, and working knowledge of most of the others: firewalls (Fortinet preferred), OT network monitoring (Nozomi, Dragos or similar), secure remote access (Xona or similar), Active Directory (Group Policy, RADIUS, LDAP), PKI, SIEM, Centralized security management platforms, application control (Trellix or similar), backup and recovery, Windows and Linux server build (hardening & virtualization), and hardening of field devices (IEDs, RTUs and gateways).
 Working proficiency in PowerShell for Windows Server and Active Directory administration. 
 Proven ability to produce security documentation that customers and auditors accept, experience training engineers and willingness to travel 20–40%, including extended site stays and ability to work across time zones.
 Desired Characteristics
 Certifications such as GICSP, GRID, ISA/IEC 62443 Cybersecurity Expert, CISSP, Fortinet FCP or FCSS (formerly NSE 4 and NSE 7) or Splunk Core Certified, or vendor training – Nozomi/Dragos.
 Experience as the cybersecurity lead on large utility, data center or industrial projects with multiple vendors and demanding customers.
 Experience building AI-assisted engineering workflows, such as prompt libraries, agent-based tools or API integrations, for documentation, requirements mapping, etc.
 Configuration-as-code and scripting experience: PowerShell DSC or Ansible, Python for Linux.
 Communicates clearly: writes procedures other engineers can follow without help, and explains and defends design decisions with both junior engineers and customer security teams.
 Holds scope boundaries with customers firmly and professionally, knowing this discipline protects both schedule and margin.
 Experience working in a global, multicultural organization. Additional languages are a plus.
 Takes ownership: when a problem appears on one project, fixes the toolkit so it does not happen again.

As a Laser Engineer, you'll design, build, and maintain the laser systems that trigger and diagnose Fuse's pulsed-power machines at our Napierville facility.

This is hands-on work: aligning and maintaining precision optical systems, developing laser triggering and diagnostic capabilities for high-energy-density experiments, and troubleshooting real hardware on a fast-moving test schedule.

 - Design, build, align, and maintain precision laser systems used for triggering and diagnostics on pulsed-power experiments.

 - Develop and improve laser-based diagnostic techniques, including timing, triggering, and optical diagnostics.

 - Troubleshoot optical and laser hardware to keep experimental systems operating and experiments on schedule.

 - Work with physics and electrical engineering teams to integrate laser systems with the broader pulsed-power platform.

 - Develop and maintain safe operating procedures for high-power laser systems and train team members on proper use.

 - Document system designs, alignment procedures, and troubleshooting methods.

 - Hands-on experience designing, building, or maintaining laser systems in a research or industrial environment.

About the team

The Fraud Countermeasures team is part of Data Science, and it's how Wealthsimple grows safely. We balance fraud losses with client friction, so legitimate clients can use their money without jumping through hoops. We work in small pods that pair a fraud countermeasures lead with a data scientist and an analytics developer, and we sit alongside Product and Engineering on every new feature launch. We use data to make every decision, and we use AI tools to move faster. If you want to work on hard problems with people who care about craft, you'll fit right in.



About the role

Card fraud is one of the highest-stakes problems at Wealthsimple, and this role owns the strategy for it. You'll set direction for how we prevent application, transaction and account takeover fraud across our card products, and you'll do it independently, with real accountability for the outcome. This is a Staff individual contributor role with manager-level impact: you'll lead through expertise and influence, not direct reports. It's open to candidates in any timezone in Canada.

 - Own fraud strategy and execution across application, transaction and account takeover fraud for Wealthsimple's card products.

 - Manage the card fraud loss budget as our volumes grow, and guard against the fraud attacks that can blow a budget up.

 - Design, backtest, ship and tune detection rules, and set decision thresholds on ML risk scores.

 - Weigh fraud losses prevented against operational cost and client experience before you recommend an approach.

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to build controls that stop fraud without blocking legitimate clients, like step-up authentication instead of a hard decline.

 - Guide the data scientists and analytics developers in your pod, and mentor junior teammates on strategy, rule building and problem-solving.

 - 6+ years of experience in fraud prevention, including 3+ years working directly on card fraud (prepaid or credit) at an issuer, fintech or payments platform.

 - Hands-on ownership of card fraud strategy across application, transaction and account takeover fraud.

 - Advanced SQL. You write complex queries against transaction-level data yourself, without waiting for an analyst to pull it.

 - A track record of building, backtesting, shipping and tuning fraud rules, and explaining the precision, catch rate and approval rate impact of each.

 - Experience quantifying fraud savings against operational and client experience costs to make a clear recommendation.

 - Experience using AI tools in your daily work, and examples of where they changed your output.

 - The ability to influence Product, Engineering, credit risk, operations and external vendors toward a decision without direct authority.

 - Clear communication with technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership.

 - Nice to have: Knowledge of Visa and Mastercard network rules, dispute processes and chargeback rails.



Who you are

 - You set direction on your own and take ownership over outcomes for your space, from fighting fraud attacks to minimizing client friction.

 - You make decisions with numbers behind them, and you're honest about what the numbers can't tell you.

 - You lead through influence. You can get a roadmap conversation to go your way by rallying others around shared objectives.

With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe.   
 SUMMARY
Jabil is seeking an experienced Senior Photonics Test Development Engineer in Ottawa, Canada. In this role, you will be responsible for developing test solutions for photonics/optics products; including developing the test strategy and test plan, selecting/sourcing test equipment and test fixtures/hardware, developing the test automation software, and deploying the completed test solutions worldwide at Jabil manufacturing sites and/or design verification labs. 
 You will work closely with customers and Jabil’s extended cross-functional teams (R&D, Manufacturing, Program Management, Quality) to deliver optimized manufacturing test solutions for both customer and Jabil-designed products.  You will also support R&D in evaluating performance of early product releases.  
 You will be a strong team player and play a critical member in defining future test strategies for the Photonics Test Engineering team at Jabil.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
 Develop manufacturing and/or design verification test plans for optimal test coverage, test time and cost efficiency. Develop test capacity analyses for product demand forecasts provided by Sales/Business Managers.
 Develop test hardware solutions including selection of test equipment and design of test fixtures/test PCBAs.
 Develop test software solutions including test automation scripts, operator GUI and data analysis using software languages such as Python, C#, MATLAB, etc.
 Verify test station operation, performance, stability and robustness.
 Perform hands-on design verification testing (DVT) of prototypes in R&D labs when requested. Maximize reuse of DVT software for subsequent manufacturing test solution.  
 Generate test documentation such as test plans, test hardware descriptions, test software requirements/descriptions, test equipment lists, test procedures, debug/troubleshooting manuals, training plans, etc.
 Provide test/diagnostics training to technicians, test operators and other test engineers as required.
 Support root cause analysis & troubleshooting activities on NPI and volume product in test. Analyze test data to determine issues with product test performance and recommend corrective actions. 
 Assist in developing budgets, quoting new projects and estimating cost impact of change requests.
 Collaborate with extended teams to develop project schedules and execute projects to completion.
MANAGEMENT & SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES
 Typically reports to Manager – Photonics Test Engineering. 
 On large projects, leads team of Test Development Engineers on Photonics Test Development Projects. Coaches and guides other team members and participates in implementing best test engineering practices throughout the organization.
JOB QUALIFICATIONS - KNOWLEDGE REQUIREMENTS
 Mandatory Requirements: 
 Demonstrated experience in the testing of photonics technology (devices, modules, line cards, shelves, etc.).
 Strong knowledge of English (both spoken and written). Able to converse on technical topics in English, and to prepare and present reports in English. 
 Good understanding of fundamental optical concepts such as optical power, optical power loss/gain, optical wavelength/spectrum, polarization, polarization dependent loss, optical signal-to-noise ratio, etc.
 Good understanding of key test and measurement concepts utilized in assessing the performance of optical transmitters, receivers and transceivers, such as bit error rate, eye diagram characterization, jitter, etc.
 Experience with standard test equipment used for test and characterization of optical products, such as bit error rate testers, optical power meters, optical amplifiers, optical spectrum analyzers, wavelength meters, etc.
 Experience developing software/test scripts using object-oriented software languages: Python (preferred), C++, etc.
 Beneficial Requirements: 
 Experience with testing photonic products with coherent optical technology.
 Experience with testing pluggable transceivers, such as SFP, QSFP, CFP2/CFP4, etc.
 Past development writing s/w used for test automation: Python, C++, C#, MATLAB, Test Stand, LabVIEW, C/C++, ATEasy, etc.
 Experience with support of manufacturing sites, where optical products are built and tested.
 Some experience with functional testing of PCBAs is desirable. 
 Good understanding of manufacturing test strategies for optical products . 
 Good understanding of the differences between manufacturing test and design verification test. 
 Experience in developing cost-effective test stations for volume manufacturing.
 General Requirements:  
 Strong root cause analysis and troubleshooting skills.
 Leader. Oversees and/or mentors others. Works well within a team environment.
 Self-starter, highly motivated and with strong desire of accountability and ownership.
 Ability to develop project schedules, budgets and track projects to completion.
 Compliance with Employee Health and Safety policies (EHS), and Corporate IT Security policy
 Willingness to travel world-wide up to 20% of the time.
 Fluent in use of standard Microsoft Office tools.

 Electrical Engineering Degree or equivalent.
 Minimum 5 years in photonics/optical test development in an R&D, EMS or OEM environment.

 Le ou la planificateur(trice) principal(e), approvisionnement joue un rôle clé dans la planification de l’approvisionnement, le réapprovisionnement des stocks, la planification des achats et la gestion de la performance des fournisseurs pour un portefeuille attitré de produits et de fournisseurs.
 Dans ce rôle, vous utiliserez des systèmes MRP/ERP, des analyses de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, des prévisions ainsi que des outils d’intelligence d’affaires afin d’assurer la disponibilité des produits, d’optimiser les niveaux de stocks, d’atténuer les risques d’approvisionnement et de soutenir la performance financière et opérationnelle.
 Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes de planification de la demande et des événements, d’approvisionnement stratégique, d’optimisation des stocks, des opérations des centres de distribution, de logistique entrante, des ventes et d’intelligence d’affaires afin de convertir les besoins liés à la demande et aux activités commerciales en stratégies efficaces d’approvisionnement et de réapprovisionnement.
 À titre de membre principal de l’équipe, vous dirigerez également des initiatives complexes, favoriserez l’amélioration continue et l’automatisation des processus, et agirez comme personne-ressource ainsi que comme mentor auprès des autres planificateurs de l’approvisionnement.
 Vos responsabilités 
 Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des plans d’approvisionnement et de réapprovisionnement des stocks pour un portefeuille attitré de produits et de fournisseurs.
 Utiliser les systèmes MRP et ERP pour générer des bons de commande et optimiser les stocks, les niveaux de service, la disponibilité des produits et le fonds de roulement.
 Analyser les données relatives à la demande, aux stocks, à la performance des fournisseurs et à la chaîne d’approvisionnement afin de cerner les risques, les pénuries, les stocks excédentaires et les occasions d’amélioration.
 Élaborer des plans d’atténuation des risques d’approvisionnement et gérer de façon proactive les exceptions, les perturbations et l’évolution des besoins de l’entreprise.
 Collaborer avec l’équipe de planification de la demande et des événements afin d’harmoniser les prévisions, les plans d’approvisionnement, les engagements envers les clients, les promotions, les besoins saisonniers et les événements commerciaux spéciaux.
 Collaborer avec l’équipe d’approvisionnement stratégique relativement aux stratégies d’achat, aux initiatives auprès des fournisseurs, aux négociations, à l’attribution des contrats et aux engagements en matière de stocks.
 Travailler en partenariat avec les équipes des opérations et d’optimisation des stocks afin d’améliorer les paramètres d’achat, le flux des stocks et l’efficacité opérationnelle.
 Gérer la performance des fournisseurs et contribuer à la résolution des enjeux liés à l’approvisionnement, aux achats et aux opérations.
 Analyser des scénarios complexes d’achat et d’investissement et recommander des approches permettant d’équilibrer les exigences financières, les besoins en stocks, la logistique, l’espace disponible et les niveaux de service.
 Diriger des initiatives interfonctionnelles d’amélioration de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, d’automatisation et d’optimisation des processus, ou y contribuer.
 Utiliser des outils comme Excel et Power BI pour analyser les données, cerner les tendances, dégager des constats et présenter des recommandations à la direction.
 Agir comme expert(e) en matière de planification de l’approvisionnement, partager les meilleures pratiques et accompagner ou encadrer les autres membres de l’équipe.
 Exigences de base 
 Diplôme pertinent ou expérience équivalente.
 Généralement, au moins 7 ans d’expérience pertinente en planification de l’approvisionnement, planification des stocks, achats, gestion de la chaîne d’approvisionnement ou dans un domaine connexe.
 Maîtrise professionnelle du français et de l’anglais, à l’oral comme à l’écrit.
 Compétences et expérience privilégiées 
 Baccalauréat en gestion de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, en administration des affaires, en gestion des opérations ou dans une discipline connexe.
 Expérience en planification de l’approvisionnement, gestion des stocks, réapprovisionnement, achats et prévision de la demande.
 Expérience avec des systèmes ERP/MRP ou des systèmes de réapprovisionnement des stocks.
 Maîtrise avancée de Microsoft Excel et expérience avec des ensembles de données volumineux ou complexes.
 Expérience avec Power BI ou d’autres outils d’intelligence d’affaires ou de visualisation de données.
 Solides capacités analytiques et expérience dans la transformation de données en recommandations d’affaires concrètes.
 Expérience dans la gestion de la performance des fournisseurs, des contraintes d’approvisionnement, des risques liés aux stocks et de la disponibilité des produits.

Who are we?

Our mission is to scale intelligence to serve humanity. We’re training and deploying frontier models for developers and enterprises who are building AI systems to power magical experiences like content generation, semantic search, RAG, and agents. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. We like to work hard and move fast to do what’s best for our customers.

Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are passionate about their craft. Each person is one of the best in the world at what they do. We believe that a diverse range of perspectives is a requirement for building great products.

Join us on our mission and shape the future!



Why this role?

We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all. Data quality is foundational to this process. Machines (or Large Language Models to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans: by way of feedback. By labeling, ranking, auditing, prompting, red teaming, and correcting output, you will improve Large Language Model’s performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere’s tech.

Cohere is looking for Data Annotation Specialists with backgrounds and skills in Trust & Safety, Content Moderation, AI model evaluation, or related fields. This role is best suited for candidates who bring strong contextual judgment, cultural and bias sensitivity, and experience applying nuanced guidelines to complex or ambiguous content. Successful candidates will be highly detail-oriented, comfortable evaluating safety risks across different user intents and scenarios, and able to make consistent, well-reasoned decisions with a high degree of independence after onboarding.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT ON THIS ROLE: In this position, you will be asked to engage with human-generated and model-generated tasks which will sometimes mean intentional exposure to explicit content. Your annotations on these explicit tasks will be used to prevent the Large Language Model from generating unintentional, adversarial, toxic, or unsafe outputs. The types of explicit content you may be exposed to may include but are not limited to those of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature.

Please Note: This is a part-time, remote, independent contractor position available within Canada or the United States. We seek candidates who are able to commit to 16 hours per week minimum at a 45 CAD/hour or 40 USD/hour contract rate, depending on your location, consisting of 30/hour base pay plus 15 CAD or 10 USD/hour hazard pay. This role is BYOD 💻 - Bring Your Own Device (laptop). 12 months contract with potential for extension.

As a Data Annotation Specialist on safety task, you will:

 - Evaluate and improve model safety: Label, rank, audit, and refine human- and model-generated text to improve safety, quality, and policy alignment, including content that may be sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing.

 - Apply nuanced safety judgment: Assess model outputs against detailed safety guidelines, rubrics, and style standards, making consistent decisions across ambiguous, sensitive, and context-dependent cases.

 - Create prompts and safety test cases: Write realistic prompts, user scenarios, and adversarial examples that help evaluate model behavior across safety categories and uncover unsafe, evasive, over-refusing, or policy-inconsistent responses.

 - Support quality and calibration: Identify annotation inconsistencies or unclear guidelines, and provide actionable feedback on recurring edge cases, model failures, and opportunities to improve data quality.

 - Work with precision and independence: Complete annotation tasks with strong attention to detail, while being comfortable working independently in a globally distributed, asynchronous team environment.

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - 1+ years of experience in Content Moderation,Trust and Safety, AI data annotation, LLM evaluation, or a related analytical role, with exposure to quality assurance, red teaming, and/or prompt engineering preferred.

 - Experience applying detailed guidelines to complex and sensitive content, with strong contextual and sociocultural judgment and the ability to recognize and manage personal bias.

 - Emotional resilience: Comfort working with content that contains unsafe, explicit, and/or toxic content, including content of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature.

 - Excellent command of written English and the ability to clearly justify content evaluations, including why an output is safe, unsafe, high-quality or low-quality. Bonus points if you are fluent in another language!

 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, with the ability to maintain consistency across high-volume and monotonous tasks.

 - Strong execution in a remote environment, including good time management, comfort using new tools, and the ability to work independently in a global, asynchronous team.



The Candidate Journey:
Initial Screening - Once you have submitted your application our Talent Team will review your resume and writing samples.
Virtual Annotation Test - This assignment will test your written skill through various language-based tasks, such as a a writing sample, interacting with a chat bot, and more.
Video Screen - If selected to move forward, you will have a short video call with a member of our Operations Team!
Offer - Independent Contractor Agreement


As an independent contractor, you maintain control over how you complete your work and may work with multiple clients simultaneously, although we ask you to declare if any of these are with a direct competitor of Cohere and maintain IP confidentiality of the Cohere project. Independent contractors are not eligible for health benefits or other benefits provided to employees. Compensation for services is provided to contractors by contractors invoicing for services provided pursuant to the terms of our agreement with the contractor.

It is important to understand that as an independent contractor, continuous work is not guaranteed. The client-contractor relationship is fundamentally project-based, meaning engagements may be temporary, periodic, or intermittent based on our organizational needs and project availability. As an independent contractor, you should anticipate fluctuations in workflow and therefore compensation for services when Cohere does not require as many hours of services in a week.

Prospective candidates, please be advised: this role involves working with human generated and model generated tasks that may involve exposure to not safe for work (NSFW) text content as part of data annotation tasks, including explicit, offensive, or other inappropriate material.

The Director, Group Benefits Risk Oversight, is responsible for providing independent second-line risk oversight and effective challenge to the Group Benefits business, with a strong focus on understanding the business, its operations, and the risks that could affect customers, plan sponsors, financial performance, regulatory obligations, and strategic objectives.
 Reporting to Canada Segment Risk, you will work closely with leaders and teams across Group Benefits, such as Disability, Health and Dental, Underwriting, Plan Administration, Product, Distribution, and Transformation. The role requires someone who can look across these areas, identify themes and interconnected risks, and provide a broader risk perspective on how business decisions, operational challenges, and change initiatives could affect Group Benefits.
 The successful candidate will combine strong knowledge of the Group Benefits business with risk management expertise, providing oversight across risk and control self assessments, issue management, change, third-party risk, operational resilience, and emerging risks.
 Position Responsibilities 
 Provide independent second-line risk oversight and effective challenge across the Group Benefits business, leveraging a strong understanding of its products, operations, strategic priorities, customer commitments, and risk profile.
 Establish strong relationships with leaders and subject matter experts across all business functions.
 Identify and assess risks arising from Group Benefits operations and business practices, such as claims management, underwriting, plan setup and administration, customer and plan sponsor servicing, and third parties.
 Look across individual issues and business areas to identify systemic risks, recurring themes, common root causes, and opportunities to strengthen the overall Group Benefits control environment.
 Assess how strategic initiatives, business transformation, technology implementations, process changes, new products, and operating model decisions could change the Group Benefits risk profile.
 Provide oversight and challenge of Group Benefits risk and control self assessments, issue and corrective action management, change risk assessments, third-party risk assessments, operational resilience, and critical operations.
 Review and challenge the adequacy of controls and mitigation strategies, with particular focus on whether they address the underlying drivers of risk and produce sustainable business outcomes.
 Monitor emerging risks and trends that could affect Group Benefits, including changes in customer expectations, workforce and capability, technology and automation, fraud, regulatory expectations, third-party dependencies, and the broader benefits and insurance environment.
 Connect risk information across Group Benefits to provide senior leaders with a forward-looking view of concentrations, trends, vulnerabilities, and emerging concerns, rather than assessing issues solely in isolation.
 Provide clear and practical risk insights to Group Benefits senior leaders and governance committees, helping management understand both individual risks and their potential broader business implications.
 Partner constructively with first-line stakeholders to strengthen risk management practices while maintaining appropriate second-line independence and effective challenge.
 Support regulatory reviews, audits, investigations, and other governance activities affecting Group Benefits.
 Bring insights from Group Benefits into the broader Canada Segment Risk organization and contribute to the continued evolution of risk frameworks, methodologies, and reporting.
 Required Qualifications: 
 8–10+ years of relevant experience in Group Benefits.
 Relevant experience in insurance operations, risk management, audit, compliance, or a related discipline.
 Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, Accounting, or a related discipline.
 Strong knowledge of the Group Benefits business and operating environment, with experience in areas such as Disability, Health & Dental, Underwriting, Plan Administration, Product, or Operations.
 Ability to understand complex end-to-end business processes and identify how risks and issues in one area can have broader implications across Group Benefits.
 Strong understanding of operational risk, controls, governance, and issue management, with the ability to apply risk principles pragmatically within a complex business.
 Demonstrated ability to provide credible, constructive challenge and influence senior business and operational leaders.
 Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to identify patterns, root causes, interconnected risks, and emerging themes from complex information.
 Ability to translate risk information into clear business implications and actionable insights for senior leadership.

 Professional designation such as CPA, CIA, CRMA, CRM, or an equivalent risk, audit, or insurance designation.

 À propos du poste 
 Nous misons sur une approche sales-led, et ce poste la rend reproductible. Le problème le plus important de l’entreprise en ce moment est de bâtir du pipeline avec de nouveaux comptes qui nous correspondent.  Publipostage et cadeaux d’affaires
 Programmes ABM : les actions ciblant la liste de comptes nommés, du premier contact jusqu’à la passation aux Ventes

 Lancer un atelier IA en personne, sur invitation, pour les comptes cibles
 Expérimenter une campagne de publipostage

 Construire les premières actions ABM sur la liste de comptes nommés, avec le CRO et les Ventes
 Faire fonctionner le podcast, les événements et la liste outbound comme une seule démarche multi-threaded, pour qu’un compte pertinent entende parler de nous plus d’une fois
 Curieux, et capable de prendre du recul. Vous tirez les fils : pourquoi, qu’est-ce qui le prouverait, quelle est la plus petite façon de le tester. Vous savez réfléchir de manière stratégique et vous forger un point de vue. Puis vous lancez l’expérience quand même.

 Dans l’action, et vous savez déléguer. Vous couvrez plus de terrain en confiant du travail à des agences, des pigistes, des agents et des collègues, et en les briefant bien.
 Le 80/20 par instinct. Vous repérez les quelques éléments à plus fort impact et commencez par là. Plus n’est pas mieux. Nous testons la version minimale viable d’une action avant d’investir dans la version complète.
 Expert d’un canal, prêt à improviser sur les autres. Vous êtes peut-être spécialiste des médias payants. Vous devrez tout de même construire de A à Z une action événementielle et une action de publipostage, et nous voulons quelqu’un qui en a envie.

 Données et instinct, en équilibre. Vous lisez les chiffres, et vous vous fiez aussi à votre lecture d’une salle, d’un compte, d’un message. Vous savez dire lequel vous avez utilisé et pourquoi.
 L’humilité intellectuelle. Vous dites facilement : « Je me suis trompé, voici ce qui m’a fait changer d’avis. » Nous vous interrogerons sur un échec dont vous êtes sincèrement fier, et sur quelque chose que vous avez construit et qui vous gêne un peu.

 Une équipe marketing restreinte, senior et très opérationnelle. Croissance et product-led growth, SEO, AEO et contenu, marque et design, et marketing produit. L’équipe grandit grâce à l’IA, pas en effectifs, par choix : chacun construit ses propres compétences et agents sur notre propre plateforme, et toutes les deux semaines, nous organisons un Marketing AI Open Hour où quelqu’un présente ce qu’il a construit. Vous rejoindrez des gens qui livrent, et qui s’attendent à ce que vous montriez aussi votre travail.

 Vous relevez du VP Croissance/Marketing, qui donne beaucoup de rétroaction et l’intègre au poste : un 1:1 de réflexion mensuel, un point de coaching tous les deux mois, et une rétroaction précise, rapide et visible. Nous nous appuyons sur les données et l’instinct, et nous essayons l’IA avant d’ajouter des gens. Vous avez l’occasion de bâtir le moteur d’acquisition d’une approche sales-led, pas d’en hériter.

 Au quotidien, vous travaillez avec le CRO et l’équipe des ventes. Vous travaillez aussi avec notre responsable des partenariats, notre responsable du design et les agences que vous gérez.

The situation, honestly
 Our content department head is going on a planned leave in the near future. Before that happens, we need a senior editor in place who can hold the line on strategy and quality while she's out, then keep raising the bar when she's back.
 This starts as a contract role with a clear path to a full-time hire based on performance . We're not being coy about it: the leave is the reason for the speed, and the contract period is a working trial on both sides. If you do well, there's a permanent senior seat here with a benefits package.
 Because of that timeline, we need someone who can ramp fast and operate independently. You'll get a real onboarding, documented strategy, and a team that knows what it's doing. You will not get six months to find your footing.
 Who we are
 RGX is a digital marketing agency built for home service businesses: HVAC, pest control, plumbing, electrical, and the trades that keep homes running.
 Our clients are not hobby businesses. They’re doing $1.5M+ in annual revenue, investing in growth.
 We help serious service businesses get clearer about what they offer, sharper about who they serve, and more direct about why a customer should choose them. Strategy first. Every sentence accountable to the business it serves.
 What you'll actually do
 Review strategy before content exists. You'll read content briefs, keyword strategies, and funnel plans before writing starts, and pressure-test them. If the targeting is off, the search intent is misread, or the funnel logic doesn't hold, you catch it at the brief stage, not the draft stage.
 Edit for strategic alignment. Every draft gets checked against the strategy it was written to serve. You'll verify the copy matches the persona, the CTA fits the funnel stage, and the content actually satisfies the search intent we're targeting.
 Create editing standards where they don't exist. If you notice a recurring writing problem, a missing tone of voice guide, or a gap in our editorial process, you build the fix. You don't wait to be asked, and you don't file it as someone else's problem. You do pause long enough to get leadership and team buy-in, because a standard only works if the people using it helped shape it. Fix what's broken, and fix it with the team rather than around them.
 Spot ranking opportunities the brief missed. You read SERPs, not just drafts. If a piece could capture a featured snippet with a structural change, or a related keyword cluster is sitting there unclaimed, you flag it and adjust.
 Run quality control. You're the last set of eyes before content ships. Clarity, flow, tone, accuracy, brand voice, and the unglamorous stuff like internal links, metadata, and formatting. You'll help formalize our QA process so quality doesn't depend on any one person being in the room.
 Give writers feedback that makes them better. Direct, specific, actionable notes that explain the strategic reasoning, not just the correction. Our writers are good. Your job is to make them sharper.
 Where this goes
 This role exists because our content department is growing faster than one director can quality-control. The interim coverage is the immediate need. The real opportunity is what comes after.
 The person who succeeds here will help build the editorial function itself: the standards, the QA program, the feedback systems that let a team scale without quality slipping. As the department grows, this seat is positioned to grow into a leadership role, including mentoring and eventually managing editors. You'll be learning team leadership directly from the content director, with real responsibility from week one rather than a title and a waiting period.
 If you're a senior editor who has hit the ceiling at your current job, this is the next rung.
 Who does well in this role
 5+ years editing strategic marketing content (SEO content, landing pages, email, PPC assets) in an agency or similar fast-moving environment. You've edited for performance outcomes, not just polish.
 You can read an SEO strategy document and find its weak points. Keyword selection, intent mapping, funnel logic, content architecture. This is fluency, not familiarity.
 You work independently by default. During the leave period, you'll be making editorial calls without a director to escalate to. You need the judgment to make those calls and the documentation habits to make them defensible.
 You're a genuine team player. Independent doesn't mean lone wolf. You'll be collaborating daily with writers, strategists, and PMs, and your feedback style needs to build trust fast.
 You're direct and kind in the same sentence. Writers should leave your edits better at their jobs, not deflated.
 You want more responsibility than your current role gives you. You've probably already been doing unofficial leadership work: mentoring writers, building processes nobody asked for, being the person the team actually goes to. You want a seat where that's the job description instead of the extra credit.
 How the role works
 Contract engagement to start, with conversion to full-time based on performance during the contract period.
 Fully remote. We'll need meaningful overlap with US Eastern Time business hours for collaboration.
 Competitive contract rate commensurate with experience ($3,000-$5,000 a month). Full-time conversion includes salary, benefits, PTO, and professional development budget.

 Genetec recherche un administrateur de sécurité réseau pour rejoindre notre équipe. À ce poste, vous contribuerez à définir, mettre en œuvre, surveiller et améliorer en permanence l'architecture de nos contrôles de sécurité réseau à travers les couches de périmètre, de segmentation interne, de cloud et d'accès basé sur l'identité. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes réseau, sécurité, infrastructure et identité afin de concevoir des modèles de réseau sécurisés, de surveiller leur efficacité et de mettre en œuvre des contrôles qui respectent les principes du « Zero Trust », tout en garantissant l'intégrité, la disponibilité et la confidentialité de notre infrastructure. 
 Votre journée en un coup d'oeil : 
 Conception d’architectures de sécurité réseau et de contrôles 
 Participer à la conception, à la mise en œuvre et à la maintenance d’architectures de sécurité réseau couvrant le périmètre, la segmentation interne, la connectivité cloud et les limites d’accès des tiers
 Définir et mettre en œuvre des modèles d’accès réseau tenant compte de l’identité, notamment les modèles SASE, SSE, ZTNA et les contrôles d’accès basés sur les utilisateurs et les appareils
 Traduire les principes du « privilège minimal » et du « Zero Trust » en conceptions pratiques de segmentation du réseau, en flux de trafic et en politiques de sécurité applicables
 Concevoir, mettre en œuvre et optimiser les configurations de pare-feu et de sécurité réseau sur les pare-feu de nouvelle génération (NGFW) de Palo Alto, CloudFlare, Azure et d’autres plateformes de sécurité
 Établir des architectures de référence, des normes de conception et de la documentation concernant la topologie du réseau, les modèles de segmentation et l’historique des modifications des règles

 Contrôles d’identité et d’accès 
 Mettre en œuvre et maintenir des contrôles d’identité au niveau du réseau, y compris des politiques de segmentation basées sur les utilisateurs et les appareils 
 Collaborer avec les équipes informatiques et de sécurité pour appliquer des politiques d’accès conditionnel au périmètre du réseau et aux passerelles VPN 
 Prendre en charge les intégrations de gestion des accès privilégiés (PAM) à la périphérie du réseau 
 Définir et maintenir des profils d’accès réseau basés sur les rôles, alignés sur les services de l’organisation et les classifications de risques 
 Collaboration et opérations de sécurité réseau 
 Veiller à ce que les exigences de sécurité soient intégrées dans la conception du réseau, la gestion des changements et les opérations quotidiennes

 Réagir aux incidents et anomalies de sécurité réseau ; effectuer des analyses des causes profondes et mettre en œuvre des mesures correctives 
 Gérer les politiques de filtrage d’URL et les flux de renseignements sur les menaces 
 Rédiger et tenir à jour la documentation de sécurité, notamment les guides d’exploitation, les schémas de réseau et les références aux politiques

 Soutenir les audits internes et externes en produisant des journaux de modifications du pare-feu, des preuves de contrôle d’accès et la documentation relative aux politiques 
 Contribuer aux critères de référence en matière de renforcement de la sécurité (CIS, NIST) et veiller à ce que les écarts soient suivis et que les risques soient acceptés de manière appropriée 
 Participer à la gestion des vulnérabilités des périphériques réseau, y compris l’application de correctifs au micrologiciel et la détection des dérives de configuration

Build something people love

Wealthsimple's mission is to help everyone achieve financial freedom – by making financial services simple, transparent, and low-cost. We're Canada's largest fintech, trusted by over 3 million clients with more than $100 billion in assets.

We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual and learn more about how we work.

About the team

The Finance team is where numbers become decisions. Within Finance, Treasury looks after the cash that moves through Wealthsimple every day — across a growing number of entities, currencies, and products. As we've expanded, so has the complexity of that job: more accounts to watch, more flows to move, more systems to keep working together. This role sits within Cash & Collateral Management and reports to the Senior Manager on that team. We're a small, high-trust group — embedded in the business, not reporting from the sidelines — and we hold ourselves to a high bar for both rigour and clarity. If you want your work to actually shape how the company operates, this is the place to do it.

About the role

Wealthsimple's cash operations have grown more complex as our product line-up has expanded — more entities, more currencies, more moving parts. This role exists to keep that complexity under control: owning the day-to-day movement and monitoring of cash, while also driving the automation work needed to make it scale. It's not a "keep the lights on" role. You'll be expected to build the tools and processes that make cash management faster and more reliable, not just operate what already exists.

This role doesn't have direct reports today, but there's real opportunity to grow into people leadership as the team scales.

 - Own the daily, business-critical money movements that power our products — making sure funds land where they need to, when they need to, across multiple entities and currencies

 - Manage short-term liquidity so there's always enough on hand to fund settlements and meet daily obligations, without idle cash sitting where it shouldn't

 - Analyze and forecast cash needs through detailed bank balance monitoring and flow-of-funds analysis — turning raw account data into decisions the business can act on, including intercompany funding requirements

 - Support new product launches by scoping their cash flow, settlement, and account requirements early

 - Scale and improve the systems we already use for cash management rather than just maintaining them — building automation for balance monitoring, transfers, and forecasting that lets the processes scale efficiently

 - Partner with product, engineering, and finance teams to keep cash operations in step with the business as it moves and expands

Skills you bring

 - 5+ years of experience in treasury, cash management, or corporate banking operations

 - Experience managing cash positioning and forecasting across multiple entities and currencies

 - Strong understanding of banking infrastructure — account structures, payment rails, and settlement processes

 - Experience leading or contributing to the automation of manual treasury or cash processes

 - Advanced Excel and SQL skills, with comfort working with large datasets to drive forecasting and analysis

 - Experience working cross-functionally with product, engineering, or finance teams to support new product launches

 - Clear communication skills — you can explain cash and treasury mechanics to people who don't work in treasury

Nice to have

 - Experience in fintech or a regulated financial services environment

 - Familiarity with treasury management systems (TMS) or ERP treasury modules

 - Exposure to building automation tools using scripting or low-code platforms (e.g., Python, SQL-based workflows)

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!




ABOUT COHERE AND NORTH

Cohere is revolutionizing enterprise AI with North, an agentic AI platform designed to securely deploy AI agents and automations within organizations' infrastructure. North empowers employees to streamline workflows, automate repetitive tasks, and unlock actionable insights while ensuring data privacy and compliance. North combines cutting-edge generative and search models with customizable integrations to drive productivity and innovation at scale.




ROLE OVERVIEW

We are seeking an Agent Harness Product Manager to own the execution layer that makes North agents reliable, capable, and production-ready. This is a role that sits at the intersection of three domains:



Agent Loop and Execution. 

Own the core agent runtime: tool orchestration, parallel execution, sub-agent delegation, sandbox code execution, and failure recovery. You will define how North agents plan and act across long, multi-step workflows and ensure the execution environment is robust enough for the most demanding enterprise tasks. You are expected to engage at the implementation level, contributing to architecture decisions alongside engineering rather than simply handing off requirements.



Context Engineering. 

Own how our Agents manage the context window as a deliberately controlled resource. This includes progressive disclosure of tools and skills, context compaction and summarization, offloading of large payloads to a persistent filesystem, and the instrumentation that keeps agents oriented across extended trajectories.



Model-Scaffolding Co-evolution. 

Own the feedback loop between North's harness and the Modeling Team. This PM is the connective tissue that makes that possible: ensuring harness design decisions are validated by Modeling before they are built, that evals are the shared bridge between both teams, and that as the harness evolves the model evolves with it.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Define and own the roadmap for North's agent harness, including the agent loop, context engineering layer, tool orchestration, sandbox execution, and sub-agent delegation

 - Serve as the primary interface between North engineering and Cohere's Modeling team, ensuring new harness capabilities are validated before being built and that neither team paints itself into a corner

 - Own North's agentic evaluation framework, ensuring evals are compatible with both the North harness and Modeling's training infrastructure, and that they serve as a reliable bridge between product and research

 - Engage enterprise customers to surface real-world agentic failures and translate findings into concrete product and model requirements

 - Partner with the agentic expert modeling team to define goals that maximize the impact of our models and prioritize model capabilities and evals most critical for delivering on those goals. Establish a clear roadmap for our agentic modeling capabilities.

 - Stay current with the open-source and commercial agent ecosystem and drive adoption decisions that keep North's architecture aligned with emerging standards.
   
   


REQUIREMENTS

 - 5+ years of product management experience as a research PM, in agentic AI systems,, or applied ML products

 - Deep understanding of agentic harnesses, including the latest paid and open source offerings.

 - Deep understanding of modern LLM agent architectures, including multi-agent systems, tool-augmented reasoning, memory and retrieval, programmatic orchestration, RAG, and long-horizon execution

 - Strong grasp of agentic evaluation design, including how to measure task completion, failure recovery, and long-horizon reliability, and how to diagnose model vs. scaffolding gaps

 - Technically deep enough to contribute to architecture decisions at the implementation level: comfortable reviewing and shaping design docs, reasoning about async execution patterns, sandboxed environments, filesystem design, and the tradeoffs that come with building harness capabilities into a production platform

 - Ability to flex between ML research conversations and engineering architecture discussions with equal fluency

 - Track record of shipping platform-layer products with demonstrated impact on reliability, performance, or capability.




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Direct experience in developing and shipping leading agentic harnesses.

 - An active practitioner of agent frameworks who regularly builds with and follows the latest developments in open-source harnesses, coding agents, and orchestration tools in both professional and personal work

 - Hands-on experience with enterprise agentic deployments: multi-tenant orchestration, tool permissioning, audit trails, and compliance requirements

 - Familiarity with infrastructure constraints relevant to enterprise deployments: on-premises environments, scalability challenges, and the operational tradeoffs of running complex agent workloads in restricted or air-gapped settings

 - Prior work at the intersection of research and product, translating nascent model capabilities into shipped product features

 - Background working within or closely alongside an ML research or post-training team.




WHY JOIN COHERE?

 - Impact: Shape how Canada's most important public institutions adopt and deploy frontier AI.

 - Innovation: Work alongside leading researchers and engineers solving complex ML challenges.

 - Growth: Competitive compensation, equity options, and opportunities for professional development.

 - Flexibility: Hybrid work model with offices in key global locations (Toronto, Montreal, New York, San Francisco, London, Paris, and Korea)




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

Media buying is now the easy part. 
 In 2026, the buying itself is piping. The levers that actually move a DTC account are creative, offer, and conversion rate, and the platform keeps getting better at rewarding whoever gets those right.
 So we don't hire media buyers. We hire marketers who buy media.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands across our service lines, 20 to 25 of them on paid media, and we spend $6-9M a month on Meta. We're hiring one person to own a handful of those accounts end to end.
 Here's what "end to end" actually means here.
 You are the account manager. We don't have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership and accountability: when you're the person answering for the account, it's your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You are the creative strategist. You do the research, you find the angles, and you write the briefs and the scripts. You direct our editors and designers rather than filing requests with them. Creative isn't a ticket you submit. It's your job.
 You build the things the account needs. If conversion rate is the bottleneck, you build the landing page. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You carry up to six accounts. That's the capacity we run at today, and the team averages about four and a half. You'll manage far fewer accounts than you would at most agencies. In exchange you get real ownership of the results and you get to work as an end to end marketer instead of one station on an assembly line.
 You can live anywhere. We're a remote team and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you're the client's point of contact and there's nobody else to cover it. The rest of your day is yours.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we'll both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 We're growing fast and we keep the bar high. 
 We believe the best media buyer today is a sharp marketer who uses AI every day. We built an internal creative analysis tool that connects to Claude, and we use Pipeboard to read and write to ad accounts and run heavy analysis. You don't need to know our stack yet. You do need to actually use AI in your work, not be afraid of it, and teach yourself what you don't know.
 What the job looks like
 Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo.
 Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working.
 Run the research before the ads. Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in this account.
 Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work. Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar.
 Ship creative on a cadence. Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness.
 Build and test landing pages. Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Report on new customer economics. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
 You're a fit if
 You've done this with real money. Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them.
 You're AI-native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying.
 You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level. Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job.
 You can communicate your ideas. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire.
 You have taste and you know when to hand off. You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows.
 You're not a fit if
 "That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary. It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 Why This Role Is Exciting
 This is not a maintenance job. You will be surrounded by people who move fast, care a lot, and take the work seriously.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets.  We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You will grow into senior strategy.  We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

 Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it. 
 Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone. 
 The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy. 
 Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact. 
 We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale. 
 Now is the moment. Join us. 
 The Opportunity 
 The Senior Firmware Engineer will contribute to the development of cutting-edge firmware for our battery energy storage systems (BESS). As a Senior Firmware Engineer, you will play a crucial role in designing, implementing, and testing the embedded software that controls the core functionality of our BESS. You will work closely with hardware engineers, power electronics engineers, and data scientists to ensure seamless integration and optimal performance. 
 Responsibilities 
 Design, develop, and maintain firmware for embedded systems used in battery energy storage systems (BESS). 
 Write clean, efficient, and well-documented code in C/C++ for micro controllers and embedded processors. 
 Implement communication protocols (e.g., CAN, Modbus, Ethernet) for data exchange between BESS components. 
 Develop and implement control algorithms for battery management systems (BMS), including cell balancing, state estimation, and fault detection. 
 Collaborate with hardware engineers to define hardware-software interfaces and ensure seamless integration. 
 Perform rigorous testing and debugging of firmware to ensure reliability, safety, and performance, develop unit testing and integration testing with HIL systems. 
 Stay up-to-date with the latest advancements in embedded systems and firmware development. 
 Contribute to the continuous improvement of Moment Energy's firmware development processes. 
 The Candidate 
 We’re looking for individuals with the following traits, skills, and experiences: 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 
 7+ years of experience in embedded firmware development, preferably in the renewable energy or automotive industries. 
 Previous experience on safety-critical software development and an understanding of relevant standards including ASIL. 
 Strong programming skills in C/C++, with a deep understanding of embedded systems concepts. 
 Experience with communication protocols (e.g., CAN, Modbus, Ethernet) and real-time operating systems (RTOS). 
 Familiarity with microcontroller architectures (e.g., ARM) and development tools. 
 Experience with debugging tools (e.g., JTAG, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers). 
 Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills. 
 Strong communication and teamwork skills. 
 Passion for clean energy and a desire to make a positive environmental impact. 
 Why join us? 
 Today, we’re delivering 5x the energy density and have all the certifications needed to ship energy independence to the world. 
 Be part of a mission-driven company focused on creating sustainable energy solutions and making a positive impact on the world. 
 Collaborate closely with passionate co-founders and a team committed to innovation and excellence. 
 Contribute to building and scaling a company from the ground up, where your work will have a direct and meaningful impact. 
 Thrive in a workplace that values collaboration, wellness, and celebrating successes, with regular company socials, fitness sessions, and more. 
 We're a fast-paced and dynamic team. 
 Every day you'll be taking on a new challenge and learning something new. You'll take on a wide breadth of tasks and contribute to disrupting the battery industry. You'll be part of a tight-knit team that is working together to save the planet! Fun, health, and wellness are incorporated into our daily schedule and we encourage all our team members to bring innovative ideas to the table to create an interactive workplace.

 Financial Growth: Employee equity and a robust RRSP matching program. 
 Comprehensive Health Coverage: Extended health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents through Manulife.
 Generous Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off plus a paid company closure between Christmas and New Year's, with a generous paid sick leave.

 Company Dinner: Weekly Tuesday dinner provided by Moment Energy. We also have a generous supply of coffee and snacks for the office! 
 Our Commitments 
 Moment Energy is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection processes, including our work environment. We especially welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, members of racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+.

 Our Values 
 Our values are key to how we show up every day at Moment Energy! We keep them in the forefront of what we do, and they’re used everywhere. We refer to them when we have tough decisions to make, we give shoutouts based on living out these values, and we include them as part of our performance reviews. 
 We have 5 core values and 1 foundational pillar (Safety is our Foundation) which lays the groundwork for everything we do. 
 Safety is our Foundation 
 We prioritize the safety of our products, customers, employees, and the general public above all else. From the workshop to the field, we maintain the highest standards for our batteries in testing manufacturing and deployment, and daily operations. Safety is not only about procedures—it is about vigilance, responsibility, and speaking up when something does not feel right.
